title: Check hybrid system warning
h1: What does the check hybrid system warning mean?
metaDesc: Check hybrid system warning on? Answer a few questions to see if it's the 12-volt battery, battery cooling, the hybrid battery or inverter, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: hybrid car wont go into ready
check hybrid system and car wont start
check hybrid system light came on while driving
intro: This message means the hybrid system's computer has found a problem somewhere in the high-voltage battery, the electric motors, the inverter or the systems that support them. It can be something simple, like a weak 12-volt battery or a blocked cooling vent, or something that needs a hybrid specialist. How the car is behaving decides how urgent it is.
safety: Never touch the orange high-voltage cables or try to open the hybrid battery.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out and call 911.
If the car loses drive power, turn on your hazard lights and steer to a safe spot.
Don't try to start the car after a crash or a flood. Tell the tow company it's a hybrid.

q_behavior.help: "READY" is the light or word on the dash that tells you a hybrid is switched on and able to drive, even when the gas engine is off.

opts.a: There's smoke, a burning smell, or it's been in a crash or flood
It shut down or lost drive power while I was driving
It won't start or won't show READY
It drives, but feels weaker or the gas engine runs much more than usual
It drives normally. Only the warning is on

q_no_ready.q: When you press the power button with your foot on the brake, what happens?

opts.a: The dash is dim, flickers, or nothing lights up
The dash lights up normally, but READY never comes on

q_clues.help: The hybrid battery has its own cooling fan. Its air intake is usually a small vent near the rear seat or in the trunk area.

opts.a: The battery charge display swings quickly between full and low
A fan is loud near the rear seat, or something is covering the vent there
The engine temperature is high, or it came on after a long drive in the heat
The 12-volt battery is old, or the car has been slow to wake up lately
None of these / I'm not sure

result.title: A high-voltage problem is possible. Get away from the car
result.now: Get everyone out and move away from the car. If there's smoke or fire, call 911 and tell them it's a hybrid.
if: If there's no smoke, still don't try to start it. Have it towed and tell the tow company it's a hybrid.
If it was in a flood, keep it parked outside and away from buildings until it's inspected.
result.why: A damaged or water-soaked high-voltage battery can short out, overheat or catch fire, sometimes hours later. This isn't something to test yourself.

causes.name: Damaged high-voltage battery or cables
causes.clues: A recent crash, or damage under the car.

causes.name: Water inside the battery or electronics
causes.clues: Flooding, deep water, or a leak into the cabin or trunk.

causes.name: Overheating inverter or battery
causes.clues: A burning smell from the rear seat area or under the hood.

result.title: The hybrid system may have shut itself down to protect itself
result.now: Get to a safe spot, put it in Park and turn it off. Have the car towed to a shop that works on hybrids.
if: If it restarts and seems fine, don't count on it. The fault that shut it down is stored and can happen again.
If the engine temperature warning is on too, don't restart it.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: When the hybrid computer sees a serious fault in the battery, inverter or motors, it can cut drive power entirely. Losing power on the road is dangerous, so it needs to be diagnosed before you drive again. A hybrid scan will show which system set the fault.

causes.name: Inverter fault or overheating
causes.clues: It shut down after a long drive or in hot weather, or the engine temperature was high.

causes.name: Failing hybrid battery
causes.clues: The battery display had been swinging quickly, or fuel economy had dropped.

causes.name: Electrical fault, including a weak 12-volt battery
causes.clues: Several warning lights came on together.

you: Take a photo of the dash with all the warnings showing.

result.title: The hybrid system appears to be blocking the car from starting
result.now: Try once more with your foot firmly on the brake. If READY still doesn't come on, have the car towed to a shop that works on hybrids.
if: If a jump to the 12-volt battery brings READY back, still get the hybrid codes read before relying on the car.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: If the dash powers up normally but READY never appears, the hybrid computer has likely found a fault it won't let you drive with. That can be a battery, inverter or insulation problem, or sometimes a weak 12-volt battery, and it needs a proper scan.

causes.name: Hybrid battery or inverter fault
causes.clues: Warnings had appeared before, or fuel economy had dropped.

causes.name: High-voltage insulation fault
causes.clues: Water exposure or a recent leak into the car.

causes.name: Weak 12-volt battery
causes.clues: The battery is old, or the car sat unused for weeks.
causes.against: If the dash lights are bright and steady, the 12-volt battery is less likely.

you: Check the owner's manual for where the 12-volt battery or jump points are.

result.title: The small 12-volt battery may be weak
result.now: Jump-start the 12-volt battery using the points shown in your owner's manual, or use a booster pack. Then get the 12-volt battery tested.
if: If READY comes on after a jump, have the 12-volt battery tested within a few days. Hybrid 12-volt batteries often fail with little warning.
If the dash lights up normally but READY still won't come on, the hybrid system has a fault. Have it towed to a shop.
If the 12-volt battery is swollen, cracked, leaking or smells like rotten eggs, don't jump it. Have it checked.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: A hybrid still uses a regular 12-volt battery to wake up its computers. When it's weak, the dash can go dim and the hybrid system may throw warnings or refuse to start. This can happen even when the large hybrid battery has no problem, so a shop will usually test the 12-volt battery first.

causes.name: Aging or drained 12-volt battery
causes.clues: The car sat for a while, the battery is over 4–5 years old, or the dash is dim.

causes.name: Loose or corroded 12-volt battery connection
causes.clues: Buildup on the terminals or a loose clamp.

causes.name: Charging problem from the hybrid system
causes.clues: The 12-volt battery keeps going flat even after replacement.

you: Find the 12-volt battery or jump points in your owner's manual.
Check the battery clamps for corrosion.

result.title: The hybrid battery may be getting weak
result.now: Have the hybrid system scanned within the next few days, ideally at a shop that works on hybrids. Drive gently until then.
if: If the car loses power sharply or a red warning appears, pull over and have it towed.
If the battery cooling vent is blocked, clear it first. Heat makes a weak battery worse.
If the engine temperature climbs toward red, pull over and turn it off.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: A hybrid battery is made of many sections. As some wear out, the battery can't hold a steady charge, so the gauge jumps around and the gas engine has to work more. The computer often flags it before it fails completely. A shop will usually compare section voltages and check the cooling fan and sensors before recommending battery work, since those can cause similar warnings.

causes.name: Worn hybrid battery sections
causes.clues: Higher mileage or an older car, worse fuel economy, and a fast-swinging charge display.

causes.name: Battery overheating from poor cooling
causes.clues: A blocked or dusty vent near the rear seat, or hot weather.

causes.name: Battery sensor or wiring fault
causes.clues: The car drives normally with no change in fuel economy.

you: Check that the battery cooling vent isn't blocked.
Compare your recent fuel economy with what you usually get.
shop: Battery cooling fan and filter check

result.title: The hybrid battery may be running hot because its cooling vent is blocked
result.now: Find the battery cooling vent (usually near the rear seat). Move anything covering it and vacuum dust or pet hair from the grille.
if: If the warning stays on after a few drives, have the battery cooling fan and filter checked.
If the car feels weaker or the gas engine runs much more than usual, get the hybrid system scanned soon.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: The hybrid battery is cooled by cabin air pulled through a small vent. A bag, jacket or layer of dust can block it, and a hot battery triggers warnings and wears out faster.

causes.name: Blocked cooling vent
causes.clues: Something was sitting on or against the rear seat, or the vent looks dusty.

causes.name: Clogged cooling fan or filter
causes.clues: The fan is loud or runs a lot, especially with pets in the car.

causes.name: Failing cooling fan
causes.clues: No fan sound at all, or a rattle from the rear.

you: Listen for the battery fan running after a drive.
shop: Cooling fan and filter cleaning or replacement

result.title: The hybrid's electric-drive cooling may not be working (inverter or engine cooling)
result.now: Pull over when it's safe, put it in Park and turn it off. Once everything has cooled, check both coolant reservoirs. Many hybrids have a separate one for the inverter. Have it checked before it's driven again, and have it towed if a reservoir is low or the engine temperature was high.
if: If the engine temperature is in the red or there's steam, pull over when it's safe and turn it off. Stay away from the radiator and reservoir caps, and have it towed.
If either reservoir is low or empty, don't top it up and drive. The reason it went low needs to be found first.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: The inverter turns battery power into motor power and gets very hot. Most hybrids cool it with its own coolant and electric pump. If that pump fails or the coolant is low, the inverter can overheat and the system flags a fault. Overheating can damage the inverter or the engine, so a shop will test the pump and pressure-test the cooling system before it's driven.

causes.name: Failed inverter coolant pump
causes.clues: The warning comes on after a few minutes of driving, especially in warm weather.

causes.name: Low inverter or engine coolant
causes.clues: A low reservoir, or pink or green drips under the front.

causes.name: Cooling fan problem
causes.clues: It's worst in slow traffic.

you: With everything cool, check the coolant level in each reservoir.
Look for coolant drips under the front of the car.

result.title: The hybrid system has a stored fault that needs a scan
result.now: Have the hybrid system scanned within the next few days, ideally at a shop that works on hybrids. Don't clear the code first. The shop needs it.
if: If the car loses power, shows a red warning or the temperature climbs, pull over and have it towed.
If the check engine or ABS light is on too, mention it. Faults elsewhere can set off the hybrid warning.
If you see smoke, smell burning plastic, or hear popping or hissing from the battery area, get everyone out, move away and call 911.
result.why: The hybrid warning covers many systems, and some faults outside the hybrid parts can trigger it too. Without other clues, the stored code is the fastest way to the real cause.

causes.name: Hybrid battery or inverter fault
causes.clues: Worse fuel economy or a weaker feel.

causes.name: Fault in another system triggering the warning
causes.clues: The check engine or ABS light is on too.

causes.name: Weak 12-volt battery
causes.clues: Slow or odd start-ups lately.

you: Check that the battery cooling vent isn't blocked.
Take a photo of all the warnings on the dash.
